question.text: Under the SEBI (FPI) Regulations, 2019, the purchase of equity shares of each company by a single FPI including its investor group shall be:

answer.text: Below 5 percent of the total paid-up equity capital on a fully diluted basis
Below 10 percent of the total paid-up equity capital on a fully diluted basis
Below 15 percent of the total paid-up equity capital on a fully diluted basis
Below 20 percent of the total paid-up equity capital on a fully diluted basis

explanation.text: The Logic: A single FPI including its investor group must remain below 10 percent of the fully diluted paid-up equity capital of each investee company under the FPI regulations. The Trap: The 5 percent figure relates to the separate SAST disclosure context and is not the FPI investment limit; the two thresholds should not be conflated. Note: If the below-10-percent threshold is breached, the excess holding must be divested within five trading days. Only on failure to divest does the entire investment of the FPI/investor group get treated as FDI.
